extracted.intended_audience: users of the Magma computer algebra system working with univariate and multivariate polynomial computations (researchers, mathematicians, advanced students)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and API-level rules for factoring and finding roots of univariate polynomials, performing Hensel lifting, and creating/manipulating multivariate polynomial rings and ideals (including Gröbner basis computations) in Magma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factorization.Al parameter selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The Factorization function for univariate polynomials has one parameter, Al, which allows the user to specify the desired factorization algorithm. The parameter has 3 possible values: "BerlekampSmall", "BerlekampLarge", and "CantorZassenhaus".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default: Al = "BerlekampSmall" if q < 25, else "BerlekampLarge". Choice affects execution time strongly and depends on the finite field size q and properties of the polynomial; example timings show large differences (BerlekampLarge much faster than BerlekampSmall and Cantor-Zassenhaus in example).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsIrreducible usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The function IsIrreducible(f) returns true if the polynomial f is irreducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be used to verify that each factor returned by Factorization is irreducible (e.g., forall{p:t in a | IsIrreducible(p) where p is t[1]} returns true).

rubrics_metrics.name: SquareFreeFactorization semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: SquareFreeFactorization(f) returns the squarefree factorization of the associate of f as a factorization sequence of (not necessarily irreducible) factors with their multiplicities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: None of the returned factors will contain the square of any non-constant polynomial.

rubrics_metrics.name: DistinctDegreeFactorization behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: DistinctDegreeFactorization(f) takes a square-free univariate polynomial over a finite field and returns a sequence of 2-tuples (degree d, product of degree-d irreducible factors of the associate of f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional parameter Degree := L restricts output to products of factors up to degree L. Example: output lists tuples <1, product>, <2, product>, etc., indicating degrees present and their combined product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resultant and Discriminant (univariate)
rubrics_metrics.description: For univariate polynomials over a domain (e.g., integers), use Resultant(f, g) and Discriminant(f) to compute the resultant and discriminant respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Resultant(x^10+1, x^5-2) over IntegerRing() returns integer 3125.

rubrics_metrics.name: HenselLift preconditions and result
rubrics_metrics.description: HenselLift(f, s, R) lifts an integer polynomial factorization s modulo prime p to a factorization modulo p^k in the polynomial ring R over ZZ/p^kZZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires a factorization s of f modulo p (sequence of polynomials over ZZ/pZZ). Returns sequence of factors over ZZ/p^kZZ which can correspond to integer factorization once k is large enough (criterion involving 2^n * sqrt(sum of squares of coefficients) given).

rubrics_metrics.name: SymmetricForm for residue-to-integer conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: When Magma coerces residue ring elements into integers it returns non-negative representatives; SymmetricForm(f, b) converts coefficients to symmetric representatives in the range {-(b div 2) .. +(b div 2)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SymmetricForm on Hensel-lifted factors to obtain symmetric integer-coefficient polynomials and then test combinations/products to reconstruct integer factorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roots(f) return format and default domain behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Roots(f) returns roots of f in its coefficient ring R as a sequence of tuples <r_i, m_i> where r_i is a root and m_i its multiplicity. If f is over the free real field, returned roots may include complex roots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Roots((x-3)^2*(x^2+9)*(x+7/2)) over RationalField() returns [<3,2>,<-7/2,1>].

rubrics_metrics.name: Roots(f, S) to find roots in extension rings
rubrics_metrics.description: Roots(f, S) finds roots of f lying in another ring S (if coefficients can be coerced into S).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for polynomial h over GF(7), Roots(h) returns roots in GF(7); using splitting field spl gives Roots(h, spl) including roots expressed in terms of field generator w.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation: use exact coefficients for free real/complex field
rubrics_metrics.description: If coefficient ring is the free real/complex field, it is recommended that coefficients be given as exact values (integers/rationals) where possible to minimize numerical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact coefficients increase the chance repeated roots are correctly identified; floating-point coefficients can split multiplicities due to roundoff (examples show (z-6/5)^4 vs (z-1.2)^4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Roots.Al algorithm selection and Digits parameter
rubrics_metrics.description: The Roots function accepts an Al parameter to choose algorithm: default "Schonhage" (Schönhage implementation), other options "Laguerre", "NewtonRaphson", and "Combination". Roots also accepts Digits to specify desired accuracy d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Schonhage used, results are correct to within absolute error 10^{-d}. For other algorithms, Roots attempts accuracy of d significant figures but not guaranteed. Default Digits is current precision of the free real field.

rubrics_metrics.name: RootsNonExact semantics and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: RootsNonExact(f) is designed for polynomials with non-exact coefficients; it returns two sequences [v1,..,vn] and [e1,..,en] of approximations and error bounds (multiplicities not provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property: |f - a(z-v1)...(z-vn)| < 10^{-d}|f|; ei provide bounds so that any perturbed polynomial within 10^{-d}|f| has roots within ei of vi. If d too small, error sequence may not be returned. Non-exact coefficients must be provided with at least d decimal places for meaningful answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monomial order specification for multivariate polynomial rings
rubrics_metrics.description: PolynomialRing(R, n, S) creates a multivariate polynomial ring with monomial order specified by string S. Important orders: "lex" (lexicographical) and "grevlex" (graded reverse lexicographical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions provided: lex compares exponent tuples lexicographically (first variable greatest); grevlex compares total degree then reverse lex tie-break with negation. If order argument omitted, default is lex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: multivariate rank-1 vs univariate polynomial ring
rubrics_metrics.description: A multivariate polynomial ring of rank 1 over R is not the same as the univariate polynomial ring over R; operations differ and many univariate-specific functions are unavailable in the rank-1 multivariate case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: use the univariate polynomial ring when computing with univariate polynomials rather than a multivariate ring of rank 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomial creation rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The only way to create a multivariate polynomial in Magma is to use an expression in the indeterminates, or to coerce an element of the coefficient ring into the polynomial ring to create a constant polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example creation and printing of polynomials shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute vs recursive access to multivariate polynomials
rubrics_metrics.description: A multivariate polynomial can be accessed in two viewpoints: absolute (as parallel lists of coefficients and monomials) and recursive (as a univariate polynomial in variable v with polynomial coefficients). Magma provides distinct functions for each viewpoint (e.g., Coefficients(f) vs Coefficients(f,i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables of access functions: Coefficients, LeadingCoefficient, Monomials, Terms, TotalDegree, and recursive counterparts Coefficients(f,i), Coefficient(f,i,k), Degree(f,i), etc. Variable may be specified by index or variable object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factorization in multivariate rings returns canonical associate and unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Factorization(f) factorizes multivariate polynomial f into powers of irreducible polynomials and returns the factorization of the canonical associate f and the unit u such that f = u * associate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For coefficient fields, associate is monic polynomial; for ZZ, associate has positive leading coefficient. Example shows Factorization returning factors and u.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsIrreducible and SquareFreeFactorization (multivariate)
rubrics_metrics.description: IsIrreducible(f) returns whether f is irreducible. SquareFreeFactorization(f) returns square-free factorization (with unit) of the canonical associate of f as a sequence of square-free factors with multiplicities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: None of the returned factors in square-free factorization contain square of non-constant polynomial. Factorization further refines to irreducibles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resultant and Discriminant for multivariate polynomials
rubrics_metrics.description: Resultant(f, g, i) (or Resultant(f,g,v)) returns the resultant of f and g with respect to variable i (or v). Discriminant(f,i) and Discriminant(f,v) compute discriminants w.r.t. an appropriate variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resultant can also be obtained by elimination ideal computations; examples show resultant of bivariate polynomials and elimination ideal basis equal to resultant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivative and Integral functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Derivative(f,i) / Derivative(f,v) compute the formal derivative of f with respect to a variable; Integral(f,i) / Integral(f,v) compute formal integrals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard formal calculus operations available for multivariate polynomials by variable index or variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal membership and normal form notion
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ideal I with basis B, a polynomial f is top-reducible w.r.t. B if a leading monomial of some g in B divides the leading monomial of f; repeated reduction yields a normal form fk which is either zero or not top-reducible. If a normal form of f w.r.t. B is zero then f ∈ I, but converse may be false unless B is a Gröbner basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides example where f ∈ I but normal form is non-zero because basis is not a Gröbner basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gröbner basis characterization and construction
rubrics_metrics.description: A basis B of an ideal I is a Gröbner basis iff for all f ∈ P, f ∈ I if and only if every normal form of f w.r.t. B is zero. The Buchberger Algorithm constructs a Gröbner basis from an arbitrary basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magma automatically computes Gröbner bases when needed; Groebner(I) forces explicit computation. Gröbner bases can be put into a unique reduced form (minimalized, reduced and sorted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Gröbner Walk to change monomial order
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma implements the Gröbner Walk algorithm to convert a Gröbner basis of an ideal from one monomial order to another (typically compute basis under easy order like grevlex then walk to final order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method often faster than plain Buchberger for final order and is automatically employed when appropriate. ChangeOrder manually applies Gröbner Walk. The Groebner procedure accepts parameter Walk := false to disable Gröbner Walk and force direct Buchberger in final order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verbose controls for Gröbner and GröbnerWalk
rubrics_metrics.description: SetVerbose("Groebner", 1) (or higher) produces verbose output for Buchberger; SetVerbose("GroebnerWalk", 1) enables verbose output for Gröbner Walk. Within GröbnerWalk the Buchberger verbose is turned off unless verbose level is 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbose output indicates steps followed by algorithms and is useful for debugging/monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal arithmetic and access functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma provides many ideal operations: I+J, I*J, I^k, ColonIdeal(I,J) or ColonIdeal(I,f), I meet J, &meet S, Generic(I), I eq J, I subset J, IsProper(I), IsZero(I), f in I, IsInRadical(f,I), NormalForm(f,I), SPolynomial(f,g), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NormalForm(f,I) returns normal form of polynomial f with respect to ideal I. Example demonstrates meet, subset tests, product equality, radical membership and that (x+y) not in I but (x+y)^2 in I for given I.
